extraction.name: ACL OCL Corpus
extraction.description: A scholarly corpus derived from the ACL Anthology to assist open scientific research in the Computational Linguistics domain. The ACL OCL integrates and enhances previous versions of the ACL Anthology by providing metadata, PDF files, citation graphs, and additional structured full texts with sections, figures, and links to a large knowledge resource (Semantic Scholar). It spans seven decades, containing 73K papers and 210K figures.
extraction.creator: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan
extraction.citeAs: Shaurya Rohatgi, Yanxia Qin, Benjamin Aw, Niranjana Unnithan, Min-Yen Kan. The ACL OCL Corpus: Advancing Open Science in Computational Linguistics. arXiv:2305.14996v2 [cs.CL] 24 Oct 2023
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The ACL OCL corpus is constructed by crawling PDF files and metadata from the ACL Anthology website, followed by full-text extraction using GROBID. Additional information is fetched using Semantic Scholar's API. Figures and tables are extracted separately using PDFFigures. The dataset undergoes annual updates by monitoring changes in URLs to identify new additions.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Physical data collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Full-text extraction from PDFs using GROBID has limitations, including missing sections (e.g., 'Limitations, Conclusions, and Future Work'), merged paragraphs, misidentified table captions, and issues with footnotes (25 footnotes missing out of 92). Figures and tables are also not fully detected (28.78% of figures and 31.58% of tables not detected).
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw data is sourced from the ACL Anthology, which provides PDF files and metadata for computational linguistics papers. Additional enrichment is done using Semantic Scholar's Academic Graph (S2AG) via its Graph API.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: PDF files are processed through GROBID for full-text extraction, with figures and tables extracted separately using PDFFigures. Metadata is enhanced using Semantic Scholar's API. The dataset is structured in S2ORC-JSON format, including metadata, authors, body text with citations, references, sections, and figures. Annual updates are performed by monitoring changes in URLs to identify new additions.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Silver-labeled topic annotations are generated using a pre-trained language model (PLM) trained on a subset of 2,545 papers with ground truth topic labels. The model predicts topics for the entire corpus, which are then integrated as silver-labeled data.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The silver-labeled topic annotations are validated by comparing the predicted topics with ground truth labels, achieving 87% accuracy on a subset of top-cited papers. The analysis highlights biases in the distribution of topics, with dominant topics like Machine Translation being overrepresented.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: GROBID, PDFFigures, Semantic Scholar Academic Graph (S2AG) API, BART-large-MNLI, SciBERT, SPECTER
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The dataset undergoes annual updates to keep it current with the ACL Anthology. Future plans include providing full-text extraction and information extraction APIs to the ACL Anthology to host the OCL data directly on the Anthology.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset enables open scientific research in computational linguistics, promoting reproducibility and accessibility. It supports trend analysis in research topics, such as the resurgence of 'Natural Language Generation' and the emergence of 'Ethics' as a new topic. The dataset also facilitates multimodal research and the development of scientific assistants.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is biased towards peer-reviewed and open-access papers from the ACL Anthology, excluding other sources like arXiv. This limits its comprehensiveness compared to larger corpora like S2ORC. Additionally, the silver-labeled topic annotations may introduce biases due to the distribution of training data, with dominant topics like Machine Translation being overrepresented.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited to peer-reviewed and open-access papers from the ACL Anthology, excluding other sources like arXiv. Full-text extraction from PDFs using GROBID has inherent limitations, including missing sections, merged paragraphs, and issues with figures and tables. The dataset is unlabeled for specific tasks, though silver labels are provided for topics. The dataset may not be suitable for tasks requiring high-quality full texts due to extraction errors.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset is designed to enable a wide range of research tasks, including temporal topic trend analysis, document-level information extraction, coreference resolution, pre-training scientific large language models, and multimodal research tasks like figure caption generation. It also supports the construction of knowledge graphs and scientific assistants.
